claims.claim: The dated kit ran read-only creation probes across 27 registry chains and retained endpoint, block, timestamp, raw response, and error class.

The five lead examples are measured controls: empty-input BLS-range dispatch, zkSync RIPEMD160 failure, Arbitrum NUMBER/header mismatch, non-Ethereum PREVRANDAO/header values, and Monad cold-access gas.

Ethereum returned CALL status 0 for empty-input controls at 0x0b-0x11, while Avalanche C-Chain, Blast, HyperEVM, and Scroll returned status 1 with two zero output words; this establishes dispatch behavior for the tested control, not valid BLS support.
The same RIPEMD160 vector returned inner CALL status 1 on Ethereum and status 0 on zkSync Era while both outer creation calls completed.
At Arbitrum block tag 0x1ec262a3, NUMBER returned 26221369 while the captured L2 header number was 516055715; Ethereum NUMBER 26221370 matched its header at 0x1901b3a.
zkSync Era returned PREVRANDAO 2500000000000000 with captured header value 0, and Avalanche C-Chain returned 1 with captured header value 0; both controls completed with header_matches=false.
The cold/warm EXTCODESIZE control measured gas delta 2614 and warm delta 114 on Ethereum, versus 10111 and 112 on Monad.

Monad documentation states a 131072-byte code-size limit, while the followup read-only candidates at 131072 and 131073 bytes returned zero; the call result alone is inconclusive because a gas cap can also produce zero.
The focused EVM-bytecode CREATE2 checks returned formula_matches=true on Ethereum, zkSync Era, and Arbitrum; the commonly cited zkSync difference applies to EraVM-native contracts.
The fixed EIP-7702 candidate is delegated on Ethereum and empty on several target endpoints; this is account state, so it is retained as state-only context and removed from the differential catalog.
The generated blog matrix includes only chains that differ from Ethereum in at least one displayed measured dimension and excludes HyperEVM NUMBER because its endpoint failed fixed-tag stability.
The probes use no-to eth_call creation code and retain raw responses, block context, endpoint, and error classification under the read-only method.
The kit distinguishes an RPC-level rejection from a VM execution failure and from a successful empty control; TRON's creation shape was rejected before VM execution.
OP and Arbitrum cross-domain sender aliasing and sequencer finality are source-backed classes requiring chain-specific messenger and finality checks.
The catalog credits mds1/evm-diff and shemnon/evm-directory at pinned revisions and describes the live-response coverage difference.

Sender aliasing, sequencer finality, rebasing balances, configured fee currencies, native-value behavior, and exact maximum code-size limits remain stateful or bounded follow-ups under the read-only rules.
Fork-gated opcode statuses and code-size boundary probes show why Ethereum compilation does not establish target-chain deployability.
Monad gasUsed/gasLimit history and cold-access pricing, together with OP/Arbitrum fee-oracle checks, show why execution gas is not a complete cross-chain quote.
Somnia returns non-zero PREVRANDAO, but its RPC header exposes no prevRandao field to compare; the catalog therefore keeps this observation doc-only and makes no security claim.
TRON rejected the creation-shaped RPC request before VM execution, while Polygon accepted BLOBHASH(0) and returned an invalid-opcode execution failure; these are distinct evidence classes.
